text: {"features":[{"evidence":"automated vulnerability-report queue into a classification and routing pipeline","name":"Vulnerability automation ownership","description":"Captures how directly and concretely the letter shows experience building systems that automate vulnerability intake, triage, or handling.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No relevant example; security interest is general or vulnerability work is not mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions security automation or queue work, but the applicant's role or the linkage to vulnerability handling is vague."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly states that they built or owned automation for vulnerability reports, triage, routing, prioritization, or deduplication."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explains the triage automation clearly enough to show ownership and impact, such as classification logic, routing design, variant analysis, or major reduction of manual work."}]},{"evidence":"Python agents act within Go-enforced permissions and audit trails","name":"Agentic tooling architecture","description":"Captures whether the applicant has designed agent-based systems similar to the role's Python agents and Go back-end infrastructure.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No agentic or autonomous-tooling experience is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions agents or automation in broad terms, but without clear design responsibility or architecture detail."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows direct experience building agentic systems or pairing agents with back-end services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes a clear agent architecture with bounded actions, supervision, permissions, auditing, or Go guardrails that show mature design thinking."}]},{"evidence":"shipped LLM-backed features with evaluation scaffolding","name":"Applied AI production maturity","description":"Captures how far the applicant goes beyond naming AI to showing real production experience with model-based systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No AI experience is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions AI interest or light exposure, but not real shipped work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States that they shipped model-backed or LLM-backed functionality in production."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows production AI maturity by pairing shipped features with evaluation, hardening, reliability work, or discussion of failure modes and trustworthiness."}]},{"evidence":"threat models, code reviews, and remediation verification","name":"Security assessment practice","description":"Captures the amount and sophistication of hands-on security assessment work described in the letter.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No security assessment work is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions assessments only vaguely, or leans on general security interest without specific activities."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes concrete assessment work such as threat modeling, service reviews, code review for vulnerability classes, or formal assessments."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows a mature assessment practice by explaining method or mindset, such as probing design assumptions, reviewing across the stack, or verifying remediation after findings."}]},{"evidence":"Python as workhorse for services, automation, and tooling","name":"Python operational depth","description":"Captures how substantial the applicant's practical Python usage is, especially for the automation layers central to this role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Python is absent or only named in passing."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Python is mentioned as one of several languages or for light scripting."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, analysis, prototypes, or services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows production-grade Python ownership, especially for internal platforms, typed or tested services, or agent layers that other engineers rely on."}]},{"evidence":"Go as principal language for production back-end systems","name":"Go backend depth","description":"Captures how central Go is to the applicant's production engineering experience.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Go is absent or its use is unclear."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Go is mentioned, but the depth of use is limited or generic."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Go is clearly a primary language used on production services or back-end systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Go is presented as central to back-end architecture, especially in systems relevant to security tooling, platform work, or agent control."}]},{"evidence":"replaced brute-force or brittle heuristics with better algorithms","name":"Algorithmic problem-solving","description":"Captures whether the letter demonstrates real fluency with data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No algorithmic strength is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement."}]},{"evidence":"builder's eye, attacker perspective, and secure defaults","name":"Security reasoning depth","description":"Captures how thoughtfully the letter explains the applicant's way of thinking about secure systems, not just that they want to work in security.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Security is mostly a keyword or destination, with little indication of how the applicant thinks about it."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Expresses sincere security interest, but methods or principles remain broad."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explains a recognizable approach, such as threat modeling, attacker perspective, guardrails, or secure-by-default design."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows mature security judgment through multiple applied principles, such as bounded autonomy, adversarial thinking, design-level reasoning, or framing security as quiet resilience."}]},{"evidence":"helping busy developers do the secure thing by default","name":"Developer-centric security orientation","description":"Captures whether the letter frames security tooling as something that should make other engineers faster, safer, and less burdened.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Little or no reference to downstream engineers or the usability of security work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Makes a general statement about helping teams or reducing manual work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicitly frames success as making secure behavior easy, default, or low-friction for other engineers."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Consistently centers downstream users through ideas like proximity to the teams served, removing friction, scaling capacity, or respecting the people who build on the tooling."}]},{"evidence":"scaling scarce security judgment across Google's development lifecycle","name":"Role-specific mission fit","description":"Captures how specifically the applicant connects their motivations and experience to this team's Google-scale security automation charter.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Expresses generic desire to work at Google or in security, with little role-specific connection."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions scale, impact, or a backend-security mix in broad terms."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly ties their background to platform security automation, vulnerability response, or development-lifecycle hardening."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows nuanced understanding of this exact role, such as treating it as central security infrastructure or as a way to scale scarce expert judgment through tooling."}]},{"evidence":"specific stories about queues, algorithms, and tools","name":"Achievement concreteness","description":"Captures how much the letter supports claims with specific examples, mechanisms, and outcomes instead of generic assertions.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Mostly lists traits, interests, or keywords with little supporting evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Includes some examples, but they remain brief, abstract, or light on outcomes."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives multiple concrete examples that show actions taken or results achieved."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Makes accomplishments easy to picture through specific mechanisms, ownership, and visible effect."}]},{"evidence":"typos, misspellings, and sentence fragments","name":"Writing polish","description":"Captures the professionalism and readability of the prose, especially spelling, grammar, and sentence construction.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent typos, misspellings, or fragments noticeably distract and weaken the application."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Some obvious errors or stiff templated phrasing are present, but the letter remains understandable."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The writing is clean and coherent, with only minor slips."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The prose is polished, fluent, and feels deliberate and ready to send."}]},{"evidence":"Security+ and OSCP certifications","name":"Security credential strength","description":"Captures the strength of formal security credentials used to substantiate security interest.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No security certification is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ that signals foundational knowledge."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Mentions an advanced hands-on credential such as OSCP that signals tested practical offensive skill."}]},{"evidence":"capture-the-flag participation with near-top finishes","name":"Offensive security practice","description":"Captures whether the applicant maintains adversarial thinking through recurring hands-on security practice outside ordinary development work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No hands-on offensive practice is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional or casual capture-the-flag participation or similar practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular ongoing capture-the-flag participation or serious self-directed offensive practice."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows unusually strong offensive engagement through high placements, repeated serious competition, or other sustained evidence of advanced practice."}]},{"evidence":"patches upstream or maintains an open-source project","name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"Captures evidence that the applicant contributes to or maintains shared engineering infrastructure beyond their employer.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No open-source contribution is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional upstream fixes or one-off patches."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular contributions or an actively used public project."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows maintainer-level responsibility, such as reviewing contributions, setting direction, or handling releases for a project with outside users."}]},{"evidence":"replicated cache, scheduler, or rate-limiter side project","name":"Personal systems project ambition","description":"Captures how substantial and role-relevant the applicant's independent technical projects are.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No personal project is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a modest utility or simple application with limited systems depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Mentions a substantial independent build that shows backend, operational, or infrastructure thinking."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Mentions a complex systems or distributed project that tackles hard issues like failover, recovery, compaction, coordination, or consistency."}]},{"evidence":"3 to 7 years testing, maintaining, and launching software","name":"Professional tenure","description":"Captures the depth of post-school software experience explicitly stated in the letter.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Roughly 2 to 3 years of experience, meeting the minimum bar but with limited time in role."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Roughly 4 to 5 years of experience, showing solid mid-level depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"6 or more years of experience, suggesting seasoned production engineering experience."}]},{"evidence":"launched 2 to 6 production services","name":"Production scope","description":"Captures how broad the applicant's direct record of testing, maintaining, and launching production services appears.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Only one or two launched or maintained services are mentioned, or the scope is vague."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Roughly three or four services are mentioned, showing repeated production ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Five or more services are mentioned, with explicit launch, maintenance, or testing responsibility."}]},{"evidence":"Bachelor's, Master's, or Doctoral degree in computer science","name":"Degree attainment","description":"Captures the level of formal academic preparation stated in the letter.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Bachelor's degree, equivalent experience, or no advanced degree is indicated."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Master's degree in a relevant technical field is indicated."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Doctoral degree in a relevant technical field is indicated."}]}]}
